clue.text: Quail served cold in Madeira, for example

indicators.note: in tells us the cold letter sits inside the drink named next

parts.note: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone is given a glass of chilled Madeira.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quail' looks like the bird served at dinner, but it is the verb, to flinch. 'served' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to shrink back in fear, the same recoil as a flinch.

clue.text: Sally has sage hand-picked

parts.note: sage means wise
crack troops are hand-picked, elite

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally grows some sage she picked herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name, but it is a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quip, a smart joke.

clue.text: Philanthropist born in the middle of Christmas?

indicators.note: in the middle of puts the born letter inside the festive word

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a generous benefactor was born at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Nobel left his fortune to found the Nobel Prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist, endowed the prizes in his will, a famous charitable bequest.

clue.text: Charge England's opening pair with confidence

parts.note: the first two letters of England are E and N
trust means confidence

explanation.surface: England's two opening batsmen face a charge with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening pair suggests cricket batsmen, but it is England's first two letters. 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to commit it to their care.

clue.text: Check direction of walkers' path

parts.note: to bridle is to restrain or check
a way is a route or direction

explanation.surface: A rambler checks which way the footpath goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridleway is a right of way for riders and pedestrians, a country track walkers use.

clue.text: Birmingham handy for an Australian wild horse?

parts.note: Brum is the informal name for Birmingham
by means near, close at hand

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Birmingham is convenient for an outback horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Brum is the nickname of Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: A brumby is a feral horse of the Australian outback.

clue.text: Di leaves vague gut feeling

indicators.note: leaves says the name departs from the longer word, so those letters are removed

parts.note: indistinct means vague
taken as written

explanation.surface: Di walks out, left with only a vague hunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is an intuitive sense, a hunch that comes without reasoning.

clue.text: Transfer funds illegally from Arundel

indicators.note: from signals the letters are made out of the town's name, rearranged

explanation.surface: Money is siphoned off illicitly out of Arundel.
explanation.walkthrough: Arundel is a town in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder money is to pass dirty cash through legitimate accounts to hide its origin.

clue.text: Unblemished joist of hardwood

parts.note: white means pure, unblemished
a beam is a joist

explanation.surface: A clean timber joist made of hardwood.
explanation.definitionFit: The whitebeam is a tree with hard, fine-grained timber.

clue.text: Tibetan oxen eating North American people!

indicators.note: eating means the oxen take the north letter inside them

parts.note: yaks are Tibetan oxen

explanation.surface: Tibetan oxen devour North American people!
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American' reads as one phrase; 'North' gives N and 'American people' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Yanks is the informal word for Americans.

clue.text: Wrench-casters in factories, in other words?

definitions.text: Wrench-casters in factories, in other words?

parts.words: Wrench-casters in factories, in other words?
parts.note: people who throw a spanner into the works, literally into factory machinery, are deliberate wreckers of plant

explanation.surface: Someone describes workers hurling tools into the machines.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'throw a spanner (wrench) in the works' is taken literally: those who wreck industrial plant on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Saboteurs deliberately damage equipment, literally throwing a spanner in the works.

clue.text: Got rid of black swelling on toe joint

indicators.note: got rid of says the black letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the big toe
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A patient has a dark swelling on the toe joint treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toe joint' reads as one phrase, but 'joint' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of two things, a junction or coupling.

clue.text: In this state does one have trouble picking out London bus relics, possibly?

definitions.text: In this state does one have trouble picking out London bus relics, possibly?

parts.words: In this state does one have trouble picking out London bus relics, possibly?
parts.note: London buses are famously red, so their relics are red objects; a person who cannot tell red from green would struggle to pick them out

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about a condition that makes old London buses hard to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: London buses are traditionally red; the condition is an inability to distinguish red, among other hues.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour blindness is a sight condition where some hues, typically red and green, cannot be told apart.

clue.text: Knowing some of Cleopatra's tutelage

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark about the teaching Cleopatra received.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing and shrewd both describe someone sharp and canny.

clue.text: Play patience

explanation.surface: Two words, a drama and a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Play is the slack allowed in a mechanism, an allowance for movement; patience is forbearance.

clue.text: They are disdainful of Priestley's dangerous angle on board

indicators.note: on, read as aboard, places the angle inside the ship that follows

parts.note: on board means aboard ship, and SS is the abbreviation for a steamship
Dangerous Corner is a play by J. B. Priestley, so his dangerous angle is a corner

explanation.surface: Critics sneer at a perilous corner in Priestley's stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention for being inside SS (steamship). J. B. Priestley was an English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who scorn are people who despise or look down on something.

clue.text: Accident to one family reveals a splinter of bone

parts.note: a spill is an accident, a fall
I is the Roman numeral for one
kin means family

explanation.surface: An accident to a single family shows a bone fracture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'reveals' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillikin is a splinter of wood or bone, as used in jackstraws.

clue.text: Ditch set incorrectly — finished by sewers?

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters of the two words are set out wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A ditch dug badly is completed by drainage sewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains; it is people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Needleworkers finish a seam by sewing it.

clue.text: It may be a measure of fire-power

definitions.text: It may be a measure of fire-power

parts.words: It may be a measure of fire-power
parts.note: fire-power is read not as military strength but as the electrical rating of an electric fire

explanation.surface: Someone describes a unit of military firepower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire-power' suggests weapons; it is the power drawn by an electric heater, rated in thousands of watts.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of a thousand watts is how the output of an electric heater is rated.

clue.text: To butter up women, be guided by the French

parts.note: to heed is to take notice of, be guided by
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: Advice to flatter women and follow French guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax with flattery, to cajole.

clue.text: Prawns I do perfunctorily as a starter

parts.note: to scamp a job is to do it carelessly or hastily

explanation.surface: A cook admits to preparing the prawn starter carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a starter' belongs to the surface, where scampi are served as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are large prawns, Norway lobsters, usually served fried in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: A hundred-and-three's unusual even in an old city!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of the number are arranged in an odd order

parts.note: the word threes, as written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Being a hundred and three is rare even in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'even in' are links. Chester is a Roman city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester was the Roman fortress Deva and keeps its medieval walls.

clue.text: Walton-on-the-Naze, possibly?

parts.note: the Essex resort is read as Izaak Walton, author of The Compleat ..., standing on the headland, a fisherman on the coast

explanation.surface: A mention of the Essex seaside town Walton-on-the-Naze.
explanation.walkthrough: Walton-on-the-Naze is an Essex resort; Izaak Walton wrote the classic book on fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Izaak Walton was the most famous of fishermen, so Walton on a headland suggests someone fishing.

clue.text: Fourth or fifth, say, for the ideal break

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a musical gap that also makes a flawless pause.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the fourth and fifth are perfect intervals; read literally the phrase is a flawless interlude.

clue.text: Build in either direction

indicators.note: in either direction says the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An instruction to build both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a structure is to construct it.

clue.text: Delicacy eaten through North Dakota?

parts.note: via means through, by way of
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: A treat consumed across North Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: A viand is an item of food, especially a choice dish.

clue.text: Adapted melody (Deutsch)

parts.note: a tune is a melody
D is the prefix of Otto Deutsch's catalogue numbers for Schubert's works

explanation.surface: A tune arranged for Schubert, catalogued by Deutsch.
explanation.walkthrough: Schubert's works are numbered by Deutsch, written D, as in D.944.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted to suit circumstances, as an engine or instrument is set up.

clue.text: Single-line caterpillar vehicle?

parts.note: a caterpillar vehicle runs on tracks; one with wheels at the front and tracks only at the back has half its running gear tracked, and a single line is half a double track

explanation.surface: Someone describes a crawler vehicle running on one track.
explanation.walkthrough: A single railway line is half of a double track, giving the military vehicle with wheels in front and caterpillar tracks behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-track is a military vehicle with front wheels and rear caterpillar tracks.

clue.text: Bonnie Prince Charlie, say, before proposal

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a tender is a formal offer or proposal

explanation.surface: Bonnie Prince Charlie is mentioned before a marriage proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie Prince Charlie, Charles Edward Stuart, was the Young Pretender, claimant to the British throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne he does not hold, as the Stuart prince was.

clue.text: Sculptor's staff at home

definitions.note: read as 'sculptor is', the 's linking definition and wordplay

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
in means at home

explanation.surface: A sculptor's workforce is at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker.
